Skagen Blade Technology provides onsite service and maintenance of blades to wind turbine manufacturers, owners and operators.

We specializes in blade inspections, retrofits and repairs on the ground or on the wind turbines, and have a fully qualified rope access team with several years of experience with blade repairs and blade surface treatment. This gives us an expertise that provides the basis for serving our customers in the best possible way.

Name: Solar Energy USA
Description:
Solar Energy USA is a renewable energy company that specializes in solar powered energy solutions including photovoltaic (PV) solar panel systems, solar thermal systems, solar attic ventilation, electric car charging stations, and energy efficient T5 lighting. We are a national design and solar installation company based in Atlanta, Georgia. Our network of engineers and installers across the US gives us collective data and information of new developments in our industry, making Solar Energy USA one of the most advanced solar panel installation companies in Georgia and the Southeast. Our locations in North Carolina, South Carolina, Florida, Texas, Colorado, Hawaii, Nevada, Vermont, Alabama, Tennessee, and Georgia allow us to utilize local employees to commission solar systems in and around the surrounding areas.

Solar Energy USA has provided PV solar energy systems and energy efficient solutions for clients in a wide variety of categories including medical office buildings, warehouse facilities, schools, churches, gas stations, automotive companies, automobile dealerships, manufacturing facilities, and many residences.

Higher fuel cost, inflation, carbon tax, seasonal pricing and many other variables are out of your control, and will continually cost you more as time goes on. Whether you are interested in solar panels to charge your electric vehicle or to offset your home or business energy usage, Solar Energy USA has the affordable solar solution for you.

Name: Sigora Home
Description:
Sigora Home was ranked 376 on the 2015 Inc. 500 list as one of America’s fastest growing companies. This ranking, which places Sigora Home as 8th among companies in the energy sector, also named the company as “The Cleanest” of those businesses that work in the field. As an Inc. 500 honoree, Sigora Home shares a pedigree with companies such as Patagonia, Microsoft, GoPro, Clif Bar, and Oracle.

Sigora is also ranked 194 out of 450 on the 2018 Top Solar Contractors list, and also ranked #1 solar contractor in Virginia!

“Our mission at Sigora is to provide the world with access to clean, reliable energy at a fair price,” says Andy Bindea, Founder. “And our strategy for accomplishing this is to exceed customer expectations, invest in our employees, and reduce carbon emissions. We consider ourselves social entrepreneurs, and that means our mission extends beyond our local markets. That’s why,” Bindea says, “we launched Sigora Haiti in April 2015 and opened an office Port-au-Prince. We have a ten-year plan to bring affordable, renewable energy to 2 million people who lack reliable electricity."

www.SigoraHome.com   |   www.SigoraHaiti.com

Name: Sigura
Description:
Sigura, a leading provider of innovative water treatment solutions, has completed a merger with Solenis. Solenis is a global producer of specialty chemicals used in water-intensive industries. The combined company creates a diversified leader in sustainable solutions, serving a range of customers around the world in consumer, industrial and pool water treatment markets.
 
Solenis currently serves two primary segments: Consumer Solutions (consumer and food packaging, graphic paper, and tissue and towel markets) and Industrial Solutions (core water treatment and wastewater markets).  Sigura's business is in the production and sale of water care solutions and value-added services for residential and commercial pool and spa applications as well as industrial markets.
 
Sigura maintains six production facilities throughout North America, South America, Europe and Africa, with 1,200 employees globally, located in all major regions. 

Sigura has top consumer brands in the residential pool care market and strong positions in high-growth Industrial & Municipal water markets. Key brands include HTH, Pulsar, poolife, GLB, Applied Biochemists, Leisure Time, Baquacil, BaquaSpa, Constant Chlor, Hypocal, and more.

Name: Ampacimon
Description:
Ampacimon is a global leader in grid monitoring solutions to optimize T&D assets.
Ampacimon’s mission “smart solutions for a dynamic grid”, is to help grid operators unlock economic and operational value from their existing infrastructure by applying a range of technology products and services that safely maximizes their capacity and usage. Ampacimon’s products address grid infrastructure challenges such as aging assets, transmissions congestion, renewable integration, interconnectors.
Ampacimon provides a range of products to T/DSOs and other energy-intensive industries to optimize high and medium voltage over-head lines, underground cables, GIS and transformers.

Name: NantEnergy
Description:
NantEnergy’s innovative Zinc-based rechargeable batteries and energy management software are fundamentally changing the way we generate, store, and use electricity. Our mission is to deliver clean energy solutions that benefit people, business and the planet, with energy storage systems that cost less, function longer, and are far better for the environment than the lead-acid batteries and diesel generators they replace. Thanks to our technology, more than 200,000 people in villages across rural Indonesia and Africa have access to electricity, while our commercial and industrial customers have seen significant reductions in their electricity demand charges, in some cases eliminating them entirely.

As we expand, we are looking for talented, high energy team players ready to grow with our company. If a fast-paced, exciting job helping to revolutionize the energy sector fits your personality and career objectives, check out our open jobs or contact us at careers@nantenergy.com

Name: Nanostone Water
Description:
At Nanostone Water, we believe in economically solving the world's water needs.  Our mission is to provide a new generation of reliable, robust ceramic UF membranes, that provide long term predictable performance at the lowest total cost of ownership for our water treatment customers.  

Nanostone Water is a membrane solutions company with a ceramic ultrafiltration module product line designed specifically for water and wastewater treatment applications. Headquartered in Waltham, MA, the company has ceramic manufacturing operations in Halberstadt, Germany.

We have a unique technology for nanoparticle ceramic coatings and a patented ceramic membrane module design.  The nanotechnology coatings provide a tight pore size distribution in the ultrafiltration range with high strength and high water permeability.

Name: Green Energy Corp
Description:
Green Energy Corp is a leader and pioneer in design and software engineering services for distributed energy generation, load management, and innovative microgrid controller solutions. GEC provides extensive engineering support and development toolkits to promote the implementation of smart grid and microgrid technologies throughout the world.

Vision
Green Energy Corp fundamental principle and core belief is to do well and do good. GEC can be successful as a company and do well in the growing market of microgrid technology, whilst being great stewards of the planet and doing good. Providing accessible, affordable energy to everyone is within reach, and we hope to supply even the most remotes corners of the world with power.

Do Well

Be the best Smart-Grid company
Build a solution for the Industry not for a Customer
Drive the Open Source ecosystem
Gain wide-scale industry adoption
Establish long-term (multi-year) customer relationships
Enable extreme growth trajectory

Do Good

Fix the grid: enable infrastructure for 21st century challenges (e.g. security, renewables, EVs)
Provide energy solutions for emerging Nations facing socio-economic crises

Visit our open source infrastructure project GreenBus   http://greenbus.io

Name: KYA-Energy GROUP
Description: KYA-ENERGY GROUP is an international company specializing in renewable energies (solar energy in particular) and energy efficiency. It is working to meet the challenge of sustainable electrification in Africa. It designs, assembles and distributes solar units for domestic and productive applications, known as solar-powered generators (KYA-SoP).

Name: Elevation
Description:
Elevation is one of the nation’s largest providers of residential solar, storage, energy efficiency, and energy intelligence technology providers. 

With a focus on ethical business practices and customer-first values, we are one of the fastest-growing companies in the country, a multiple-year Department of Energy contractor of the year, and recognized as one of the best places to work.  

Our services also include energy efficiency retrofitting of homes, branch-level energy metering, and remote visibility through our Curb Energy division and Virtual Power Plant solutions.

By ‘Elevating the Home Energy Experience’ we are leading the transition to clean energy and energy efficiency for consumers, utilities, and enterprises.  

We offer the following:

Residential Solar and Storage: Turnkey deployment of residential solar and storage across our multi-state footprint that includes Arizona, California, North and South Carolina, Florida, Nevada, and Texas.

Distributed Energy & Grid Solutions: Aggregated smart homes with metering and control along with smart algorithms to monitor and manage energy consumption, help the homeowner reduce energy expense and shift demand to allow utilities to implement continuous Virtual Power Plant solutions and Active Demand Management strategies.

Data & Diagnostics: Through our Curb Energy technology we provide customers and utilities with real-time visibility to home energy consumption and breaker level detail that enables advanced demand management and HVAC predictive analytics.

Name: Yaskawa Solectria Solar
Description: Yaskawa Solectria Solar, a wholly owned subsidiary of Yaskawa America, Inc., is the largest U.S.-based inverter manufacturer, with design and engineering offices in Lawrence, MA, and world-class production facilities in Buffalo Grove, IL and Franklin, WI. With over 20+ years of experience Yaskawa Solectria Solar is the only PV inverter designed, made, and serviced in the USA.   The company’s flagship American-made product line, the Solectria XGI 1500 inverters, along with the XGI 1500-1MW Series Inverters, a full lineup of string combiners designed for the XGI inverters, 1-2MW factory-integrated Power Racks, and DC-coupled and AC-coupled storage solutions complete the product family.  With this full product solution offering Yaskawa Solectria Solar remains committed to delivering the highest-quality solar inverters and driving innovation in the industry.

Name: Lightshift Energy
Description: Lightshift Energy, formerly Delorean Power, is a utility-scale energy storage development company that is transforming the way utilities manage and distribute power. Specializing in innovative solutions that save costs and improve reliability for energy providers and their customers, we’re committed to bringing new investment in cutting-edge battery storage technology across US communities.

Name: EnBW North America (acquired by TotalEnergies)
Description:
EnBW North America is more than a clean energy company. We are a partner, committed to working together to solve unique energy challenges. We are focused on delivering lasting clean energy solutions that will help individuals, businesses, and governments achieve shared climate goals to improve public health and economic opportunity. We do this through collaboration and innovation, designing and building a better energy future for us all.

We’re on a mission to ensure our clean energy solutions and business operations work toward greater public health and economic opportunity for all. Our parent company has a history of imagining and building a better energy future to meet local and national clean energy challenges – we bring that same drive and creativity to meet the unique needs of the US. From floating offshore wind technology to battery storage, we are innovating our way to a smarter, more inclusive renewable energy industry.

Currently we’re advancing offshore wind projects on both coasts of the US to power communities with clean, reliable energy.

Name: NXTGEN Clean Energy Solutions
Description:
NXTGEN Clean Energy Solutions is your one-stop shop for solar energy, wind energy, battery storage, electric vehicle charging and solar lighting. We provide consultation and full project development of Clean Energy Solutions for end-user customers to help them save money, generate revenue, or both, all while reducing the carbon footprint and helping the environment.

NXTGEN provides development assistance to identify which Clean Energy options are the best fit for each client. A customized approach takes into consideration client needs including energy requirements, budgets, property dynamics, schedules, and the like, which allows NXTGEN to recommend solar, wind, battery storage, electric vehicle charging stations, solar lighting, or a combination of these technologies for a maximized ROI.

NXTGEN represents the client and manages specialty design/installation contractors and technology providers to deliver zero-hassle Clean Energy Solutions.

Name: Business Council for Sustainable Energy (BCSE)
Description: The Business Council for Sustainable Energy (BCSE) is a coalition of companies and trade associations from the energy efficiency, natural gas and renewable energy sectors. The BCSE advocates for policies at the state, national and international levels that increase the use of commercially available clean energy technologies and create a more secure, sustainable and diversified energy portfolio. The industry vision that established the BCSE in 1992 continues today, as the Council’s industries work together to meet U.S. energy needs and power the American economy.
Location: Washington, D.c., District Of Columbia, Washington, United States

Name: EcoFasten
Description: EcoFasten has established a reputation for being one of the industry’s leading innovators by providing expert solutions for mounting solar PV on any roof. EcoFasten’s broad portfolio of solar rooftop mounting systems and attachments stems from the direct needs of solar PV installers. EcoFasten takes pride in providing the right solution for every application.

Name: Emrgy Inc.
Description:
Emrgy designs and deploys modular, scalable hydroelectric solutions without the need for construction or dams. Compared to intermittent solutions like solar and wind, the controllable nature of these waterways enable higher capacity factors, do not require adjacent technologies such as storage, and ultimately deliver quicker and greater value to the customer. While in-canal hydro market potential has not been adequately quantified to date, the US market conservatively represents >6GW of undeveloped potential. Emrgy has developed a proprietary, global resource assessment tool to better characterize and quantify the vast, immediately available in-conduit hydroelectric potential.

Emrgy's turbine arrays empower our customers to monetize the energy content of their existing waterway asset that is otherwise ignored. We partnered with the City of Atlanta & Southern Company to showcase technological capabilities of the product in 2016, and in 2017 the Company partnered with Denver Water & The Bureau of Reclamation to install the first array of distributed hydropower in the United States.

Name: Clean Energy Business Network (CEBN)
Description: The Clean Energy Business Network (CEBN) works to grow the clean energy economy through policy, public education, and business support for energy companies. The CEBN's reach spans 8,000+ clean energy professionals across the U.S. and internationally, primarily representing small- and medium-size energy companies. Started in 2009 by The Pew Charitable Trusts, the CEBN is now a division of the Business Council for Sustainable Energy. Visit www.cebn.org to learn more about CEBN membership and join.

Name: Greenspot Smart Mobility
Description:
Greenspot works with municipalities and landlords to address the future challenges of urban mobility. Greenspot provides services and solutions that will revolutionize the way we commute – making it more economical, sustainable, efficient and reliable.
Urban dwellers and millennials don’t want to own a vehicle that sits idle for 95% of the time, and are therefore resorting to more fundamentally sustainable alternatives such as car sharing and electric vehicles. 

We are creating a long-term solution to accommodate these changes and revolutionize urban mobility.
Location: Jersey City, New Jersey, United States

Name: BMTA&C Energy
Description: BMTA&C is a deep tech and impact focused startup developing a breakthrough clean refrigeration technology. We are decarbonizing the cooling industry while being cost competitive.

Name: Solar Topps
Description:
Based out of Phoenix, Solar Topps was founded in pursuit of helping everyone make smarter financial decisions when it came to their energy independence. We aren't roofers, electricians, or salespeople that decided to get into the solar industry, we are a local, NABCEP-certified engineering firm that specializes in designing, installing, and servicing rooftop, ground mount, and shade structure solar systems for homes and businesses. 

Our promise is simple: to always do right by you. The critical difference with our company is that if solar does not make sense for you, we will let you know. We value an honest and open relationship over a sale. Our simple energy management solutions provide the best value in Solar, Battery Backup and EV Charging options designed to fit your lifestyle, today and tomorrow. 

By choosing Solar Topps, you have the peace of mind that your system will use premium products that are precisely engineered and installed to deliver premium results. The only thing that isn't premium about us is our price. But it is not just our prices that make us one of Arizona's best. It's our industry-recognized performance, project management, well-functioning systems, and, when needed, service. For us, it's all about top-notch customer experiences. 

We hire, train and use only our installers, not third-party contractors. We provide our crews with the right tools and fully loaded trucks, so they can get the job done right, the first time. With a reduced need to revisit sites multiple times, we are able to help our customers save more. We develop relationships with key decision-makers at the Utility, City, and HOAs to ensure projects go smoother. We cultivate relationships with our customers, making sure they are happy before, during, and after the installation process, doing our best to reduce any amount of downtime. That's the Solar Topps difference.

Get your energy, your way. Whether online, over the phone or in-person, our team is ready to work with you.

Name: Alpha Eden - Your Local Pest Control Experts
Description:
Alpha Eden a Western Exterminator Company. Pests are not only a nuisance, but they can damage your business's reputation. Our state licensed technicians specialize in Bird Control, Bed Bug Control, Vegetation Management Services, General Pest Services, Crawl Space Restorations and much more.

Alpha Eden has been serving the northwest for 30 years. Contact us to resolve your pest control issues! 877-257-4776 or email us at info@alphaedenpest.com.

Name: Kenesjay Green Limited
Description:
An energy revolution company, leading the way in creating Unlimited
Possibilities for a Sustainable World.
Kenesjay Green Limited is a locally owned sustainable energy firm and is the newest member of the Kenesjay Group of Companies. Committed to leading the way to the Caribbean's energy transition, Kenesjay Green Limited is dedicated to developing a pipeline of viable decarbonising and green project opportunities, which will create pioneering first-mover advantages for Trinidad and Tobago.

The NewGen Hydrogen Project is the first major initiative of Kenesjay Green Ltd. NewGen Energy Limited is currently 100% locally owned by Kenesjay Green.

Name: Sunbridge Solar
Description:
We at Sunbridge Solar are a globally-minded solar electric company based out of the Portland-Vancouver area. Our main emphasis is on designing and installing superior quality solar arrays for both residential and agricultural settings in the Pacific Northwest. While we pride ourselves highly on our second-to-none installations here in Oregon and Washington, our goal for meaningful local and global impact is much broader than our bottom line.

The name itself suggests the meaning we wish to convey: We’re building solar bridges in the communities in which we live and thrive. Whether that bridge be an easier and more environmentally conscious way to get power to a home here in the Northwest, or to help bring a hospital in rural Nepal into the 21st century so they can better help the more than 30,000 people that walk through their doors, Sunbridge Solar will be ready to help. The name Sunbridge Solar helps keep our mission of bringing ecologically and monetarily affordable energy to people, in both big ways and small, in mind every day.

So whether you are a homeowner looking to do something to cut your electric bill costs, a farm trying to embrace sustainability, a business looking to make a sound financial investment, or a humanitarian with a heart for changing the environment, we are here to guide you through the process.

Name: Olokun Minerals
Description:
Olokun Minerals aims to solve for global clean water security by sustainably harvesting ocean minerals from desalination brine to create a renewable source of power and provide key compounds for the supply chains of the future. 

As water demand increases and sea levels rise, desalination becomes a more sought-after solution to provide clean water to coastal communities, but it produces a brine waste three times saltier than the ocean that threatens sea life. Olokun Minerals seeks to capture that brine stream before it goes into the ocean and harvest minerals needed for transportation infrastructure and renewable energy supply chains.

What is locally sourced, certified renewable energy?

Local renewable energy sources include solar, wind, small hydro and more.  These sources supply the electrical grid with clean energy where it is consumed by users on the same grid. Shortening transmission distances reduces stress on the grid – improving efficiency and making it more resilient. Even more importantly, adding locally sourced renewable energy to the grid makes it more accessible to all energy consumers in that community. Expanding local renewable energy production also lessens reliance on fossil fuels that contribute to global warming. At CER we believe in thinking globally and acting locally.


Why should my company support local renewable energy production?

When a company supports expansion of local renewable energy production, the whole community reaps the benefits: clean energy access and usage grows, the energy grid becomes more resilient and local economies grow. CER’s Local Green Program can become an integral part of a company’s sustainability initiative with virtually zero cost and it demonstrates good community citizenship that impacts customers, employees and the community at large. Some companies will even enjoy an energy cost savings when they commit to supporting local renewable energy.

The CER Local Green Program is the first of its kind, and it is no cost to our customers.

The bad news is that there are many people and companies trying to “surf” the green wave without sufficient credibility or training to help you do your project correctly.

That is why we are here. To help separate the real green products, professionals and procedures from all the “greenwashing” that is taking place.

Welcome to an adventure that hopefully will change the way you think about HOME!

A green home on the other hand is designed with intention to function as a system, much as your car is a system of parts and pieces that work in concert with each other. Name: PECI
Description:
PECI has three decades of history helping communities and clients adopt innovative energy programs, train workforces in new technology and deliver high-touch solutions at the nexus of community and energy.  Over 35 years, we have evolved to help communities across the country identify ways to meet the future and promote growth and independence. 


NEW ECONOMY – People go where opportunity lives

Drivers of economic growth in American communities have undergone dramatic change in past decades. Changes in the economy, energy markets and technology are creating the means to bring energy system benefits directly into local communities. 


ENERGY – Everyone, everywhere needs it
 
Energy systems are at the core of community vitality – and economic activity. Stable and resilient energy systems are the bedrock on which essential economic drivers like education, training, technology transfer and growth rest.

 
COMMUNITY ENERGY – More than just electrons and BTUs

The energy needs of every community vary and they change. But what many communities have in common is that the production of energy used to serve growth, development and commerce come from sources outside of the community.  We see energy projects as a means to not only create and manage energy, but also to utilize local infrastructure to support workforce development, technology training and other community values. 

For example, reliance on power from large generation sources might translate into a lower cost for electrons, but the tradeoff comes in the form of efficiency losses, less responsiveness to local needs, lost opportunities for the maintenance and operations jobs within the community, and fewer technical training opportunities for local tradespeople and youth.

We believe that building local energy systems within local communities will strengthen local economies, make local business and civic functions more resilient and benefitting the environment.

Name: Transatomic Power
Description:
Our pioneering energy technology generates clean, safe and affordable nuclear power.

LET'S THINK RADICALLY DIFFERENTLY
The nuclear industry of the 1950s was defined by an inexhaustible optimism and rigorous scientific thinking. Anything was possible, and nuclear energy promised to power the world. Revolutionary designs were prolific. Today, however, this technological diversity has been narrowed, and the industry has become locked into one design: the light water reactor. We’re challenging this strategy and have returned to the beginning to explore another path, and another design – the molten salt reactor. This simple reactor design, updated with modern technology and materials, has the potential to revolutionize the nuclear industry.

LET’S CREATE ABUNDANT ENERGY THAT IS CLEAN, RELIABLE, AND CHEAPER THAN FOSSIL FUELS.
Our reactor generates carbon-free electricity at a price that is less expensive than coal. We can replace the coal plants coming offline in the US, and serve as an alternative to new coal plants being built internationally. We are a low-cost, environmentally-friendly alternative to fossil fuels, and we can power the world while keeping it clean.

LET’S BE SAFE.
The scientific genius of the molten salt reactor design is that it is inherently safe, as proven at the Oak Ridge National Laboratory in the 1960s. Unlike light water reactors, the design doesn’t require a constant supply of external electric power to pump water over their core to keep them from heating up catastrophically. If our reactor were to lose external electric power, and even if there were no operators on site, its fuel would drain via gravity and naturally freeze solid. In addition, our system operates at atmospheric pressure which means that there is no driving force to push the reactor material beyond the site boundary.

Description:

Safe and Secure Information Destruction

If you want your computer recycled safely and your data destroyed, Great Lakes Electronics is the company you have been looking for. The demanufacturing process takes old electronics (computers, servers, cable boxes, TVs and more) and breaks them down into their various components. Anything that contains personal, proprietary, or sensitive information is destroyed in the companies giant shredder and other components are recycled.

Great Lakes Electronics has a ZERO LANDFILL Policy

The volume of old or obsolete computers and electronics increases dramatically every year. The National Safety Council estimated that over 500 million PC's have been relegated to scrap in the United States as of 2007. These old PC's contain hazardous amounts of toxic heavy metals including lead, cadmium and mercury, and it is critical to the environment to keep these materials from landfills and incinerators.

Through environmentally responsible disposal, GLE helps you turn these liabilities into assets. Components of value are allocated for reuse or recovery of raw materials. Remaining scraps are then properly recycled by permitted associate facilities– even if it costs GLE to do it. Items of environmental concern include batteries, soldered circuit boards, cathode ray tubes and mercury wetted switches.

We recycle all types of electronic equipment containing circuit boards, cathode ray tubes, ferrous and non-ferrous metals. No minimum shipments.

Name: Dynamic Water Technologies
Description:
Dynamic Water Technologies (DWT) has changed the world of process water treatment with their internationally patented and patent pending technologies that utilize controlled electrolysis instead of chemicals to manage scaling, corrosion, and bio-contamination

Water Savings:
Make-up water savings of 15-60%
Sewer savings of 50-95%

Scale Control:
The DC process creates a controlled, partial electrolysis in the water. This process precipitates scale-forming minerals within the controlled environment of the DWT reactor instead of on heat transfer surfaces.

Corrosion Control:
The DWT process increases the cycles of concentration, allowing the minerals to remain in the water. These minerals act as a natural buffer to corrosion. The resultant water is alkaline and non-corrosive.

Elimination of Hazardous Chemicals: 
Electrochemical treatment can eliminate the need for toxic chemicals 100% 

Controls Biologics:
The system activates the chlorides naturally present in the water, creating chlorine, which acts as a biocide.

How Electrochemical Technology Works: 
A carefully controlled partial electrolysis splits water into H+ and OH- ions inside the reactor, lowering the pH and leading to a high concentration of bicarbonate ions and accelerating the precipitation of hard minerals inside the reactor. Equilibrium is maintained between the pH and alkalinity to minimize corrosion, allowing a significant increase in the cycles of concentration and minimizing blowdown to save water. Controlling scale and biologics results in cleaner heat transfer surfaces and reduced energy consumption. 

DWT Customers Include:
NASA, CARVANA, CITY OF LOS ANGELES, KAISER PERMANENTE, LA DWP, ROCHE MOLECULAR, SOCALGAS, STATE FARM, ANGLO-AMERICAN, BARRICK GOLD

The DWT process has been verified by the United States national Renewable Energy Laboratory (NREL), the U.S. Department of Energy and the U.S. Government Services Agency (GSA).

Lean & Green MichiganTM is one of America’s first statewide Property Assessed Clean Energy (PACE) initiatives – and Michigan’s marketplace for energy efficiency and renewable energy financing.

We help commercial, industrial and multi-family property owners finance energy projects, eliminate waste and save money through innovative financing solutions that make energy projects profitable for all parties – property owners, contractors, financial institutions, and even municipalities which experience a growing tax base.

Lean & Green MichiganTM is a public-private partnership that uses Michigan's new PACE statute but takes a market-based approach to energy finance and economic development. In essence, we leverage the PACE statute to maximum effect by using private capital to solve companies' energy problems, to create work for contractors, and to green our communities.

Counties, cities and townships host the Lean & Green MichiganTM PACE district, but they pay nothing to initiate the program or for ongoing program administration and bear no risk.

Property owners, contractors and financial institutions get a free market in which to arrange energy deals that pencil out for all involved, using the PACE financing mechanism to lower the cost of capital and create positive cash flow from day one.

By creating a statewide district, Lean & Green MichiganTM creates one set of efficient and flexible rules that bring maximum benefit to all parties.

Even as Lean & Green MichiganTM is propagating Property Assessed Clean Energy, it is important to understand that PACE will not work for every property owner in every situation. We are committed to helping property owners and other parties find the energy efficiency or renewable energy financing solution that best meets their needs.

Additionally, CFRW plays a key coordination role in the Cape Fear River Partnership which is focused on fisheries restoration in the Cape Fear River.

We offer multiple opportunities for citizen engagement through our citizen science Creekwatchers program, monthly seminars, paddles and clean-ups.  We provide education to both children and adults through eco-tours and summer camps.  We also manage the Greenfield Lake boathouse at a Wilmington city park, which gives the community access to the lake on paddle boats, kayaks and canoes.

CFRW is an active member of the worldwide Waterkeeper Alliance, the world’s largest and fastest growing nonprofit solely focused on clean water.  Our full time RiverKeeper, Kemp Burdette was recently recognized by the alliance as a “Waterkeeper Warrior” as an individuals that has fought and won some of the most significant clean water battles of the past 20 years.

We were honored in 2019 to be named “Conservation Organization of the Year.”

Description:
Rubbintec addresses the enormous global tire waste problem and makes rubber sustainable by converting end of life tire rubber back into high quality virgin rubber  that can then be used as a rubber substitute in a $41 billion market including footwear outsoles, tire retreads, automotive parts and many dozens of different rubber products.  We also add waste plastic to the recovered virgin rubber, which creates a co-polymer or thermoplastic elastomer, which can be used as an asphalt "modifier" to extend the life of roads and roofing materials and which can be used in many other applications.

How our Process Works:
Most end of life tires are landfilled or incinerated for energy recovery.  It is difficult to recycle and reuse rubber because rubber has been cured through the vulcanization process.    Rubbintec efficiently reverses the vulcanization process process allowing us to recover high quality virgin rubber.

Our competitive advantage is that our patented de-vulcanization technology selectively breaks sulfur bonds without damaging the rubber. This significant technological achievement enables the continuous upcycling and reuse of rubber waste, boosting the circular economy.

Many other devulcanization technologies. damage the rubber and/or utilize too much energy in their process. Having said that, Rubbintec is not competition against other devulcanization technologies. Instead, we want to replace natural rubber (latex) and petroleum based synthetic rubbers, both of which have a significant carbon footprint.

Our team collectively has over 180 years of experience in business, manufacturing, science and startups.

Join us in solving the global waste tire problem and making tire and industrial rubber sustainable.

Name: Architectural Solar Association
Description:
The Architectural Solar Association (ASA) is a industry advocate for product certification, standards development, education & training, legislative regulations, building & energy codes and solar architecture design specification as they relate to architectural solar including BAPV , BIPV and other solar building materials and trades. Our goal is to transform building facades and other architectural surfaces into generating assets.

ASA is currently focused on the following three (3) key issues:

UL Standards for Architectural Solar - UL 1703 currently has several limitations that do not address the needs of the architectural solar market.  ASA is a voice for the industry to help guide UL to standards that keep architectural solar in mind.  In the interim we plan to work with UL to establish amendments to UL 1703 with an end goal of establishing an entirely new standard for BIPV / architectural solar.  This new standard would break down the barriers to architectural solar by focusing on a family recipe approach that is analogous to other building envelope standards and the IEC solar standards of Europe. 

Financial Barriers of Architectural Solar - ASA is committed to bringing industry together to break down the financial barriers of Architectural Solar.  Currently there is significant room for interpretation in the tax code and how it applies to BIPV.  ASA looks to fund efforts to establish a sound methodology for analyzing the financial viability of projects.  ASA also looks to identify funding sources for architectural solar and connect them with our members.   

Education - ASA seeks to educate the building industry on how solar technologies can be integrated into the building envelope.  ASA believes that the building industry as a whole needs to be involved with the adoption of architectural solar. 

These focus issues will be refined and expanded as ASA membership increases and ASA Working Groups are established

– World-class equipment and platforms to scale-up and test solar and energy storage devices and manufacturing processes, including those for flexible electronics, 3D printing, and other methods of additive manufacturing

– Extensive microscopy, metrology, surface, fluids, and compositional rapid characterization tools along with full battery and solar cell and module testing

– Environmental module and product testing

– Real-time digital simulator and hardware-in-the-loop systems to evaluate power controls and microgrid models

– On-site research scientists to assist with training and testing; Testbeds users retain all rights to the intellectual property they develop at the Testbeds

– Classrooms and office space for meetings and workshops

– Entrepreneur-in-Residence and Investor-in-Residence programs to foster healthy growth of early-stage cleantech and clean energy companies

– A pay-as-you-go, open access business model for equipment time, facilities, and staff expertise

And that’s exactly what our advanced bipolar battery technology achieves.
Over the last decade, we have re-engineered how batteries are designed and manufactured. The result is the most affordable energy solution that can be implemented across the globe. Description:
Energy poverty (lack of access to electricity) is an issue facing over 1 billion people in the world. To charge a cell phone, their only form of communication beyond their village, they must also travel many hours, or even days, and pay someone for electricity..

Solar lanterns and solar home systems provide clean, high-quality lighting and cell phone charging capabilities at an affordable price. These products significantly increase the quality of life for families living in rural areas and provide economic, health, educational, and time-saving benefits. Solar energy is also good for the environment because it does not produce emissions that contribute to global climate change.

Founded in 2011, GBF has worked in nine different countries and deployed over 70,000 lamps, impacting the lives of 350,000 people. GBF is currently focusing its efforts in Guatemala and Peru, working in alliance with local not-for-profit Amigos de la Aldea.

Name: Last Resorts
Description:
Last Resorts is developing the operating systems, templates, and technologies required to deploy greenfield communities at scale.

We can't call any individual community successful until that success has been replicated countless times. Population migrations due to climate and economic stresses will present a burden beyond the capabilities of existing towns, cities, and their infrastructure, planning, and governance systems. This is an existential crisis and an opportunity.

Can we distill and reimagine from our knowledge and technology a new set of building blocks that is regenerative, sustainable, and more humane in which we can thrive instead of just survive? Substantial progress has been made in containerizing water, food, and power. The greatest hurdles that remain are a fundamental rethinking of construction and governance.

Construction is the single greatest consumer of energy in an economy. And ultimately, it is a great source of waste. Current methodologies rely on an endless supply of raw materials and a bottomless hole to dump them in when done. Every building in existence is future landfill with no meaningful ability to be reused or recycled. Recycling should be considered the least desirable outcome given inherent losses and energy consumption. We are focusing on reuse and reconfiguration by defining a new durable set of highly adaptable building blocks.

Governance has failed all but the very few at the top. An unchecked, winner-takes-all system is analogous to a biological system without defenses: cancer will spread, subvert vital resources, and ultimately kill the host. Adapting simple self-balancing rule-sets derived from observing systems of scale and bio-mimicry, communities will be able to derive unique local governance without risking tyranny, apartheid, and collapse.

Our planet rotates on its axis in a daily cycle.  Every point on the earth experiences a change in air temperature as that spot rotates to a position that faces the sun and then rotates to a position that faces away from the sun.  A massive supply of energy from the sun increases the temperature of the air during the day and then the temperature decreases during the night.
The innovation of Gravaton acts to capture the energy of the sun contained within the air and converts that energy into stored potential energy that can be released to produce an un-interruptible source of on-demand electricity. 
Gravaton’s innovation features the following benefits:
•	Environmentally friendly - use of the innovation produces no air, water or land pollution
•	Distributed power - may produce energy at any location anywhere on our planet

Description:
GogoEco retails recycled material products to city and county governments.  

As a nation, in 2014, we collected 258.5 million tons of waste.  Our landfills received 136 million tons, (65%) and we collected 89.4 million tons (34.6%)  to be recycled.  Of the recycled, at least 25% was not usable by Reclaimers and was sent back to landfills.  There are many ways that we can improve on these percentages, but the single, best way is to further develop the market for recycled material products.  If there isn’t a market for recycled material products then there is no reason to recycle.

Our City and County governments are in a position through their purchasing decisions, acting as visible examples, and legislation to lead their communities in the use of recycled material products.  

At the same time, cities face net losses to support recycling, heavy capital investments to improve sorting technology, and community backlash for restricting certain plastics.  

Cities and counties need our support.  Generally, recycled material products are offered as secondary products.  The perception for decades has been that these products are inferior.  GogoEco brings these products to the forefront and highlights their value by focusing on high-caliber commercial products suitable for city and county government at an extraordinary value.  Priced comparable to Non-Eco-Friendly products, we hope to encourage the trial and adoption of recycled material products by our governments.

As a nation, it’s admirable how far our cities and counties have taken us in the adoption of recycling programs over the last 30 years.  Further developing the recycled products markets will resolve many of the hurdles still in our way.  

GogoEco is enthusiastic about our part in the development of this essential market.  There are many ways for eco-minded individuals to join GogoEco.  If you'd like to do so, please contact us, we would love to discuss opportunities.

A paixão que move nosso fundador e  presidente – Monsieur Pierre PASSOT é a vida marinha.

Francês, oceanógrafo por formação acadêmica, mergulhador escafandrista e pesquisador comprometido, esteve e está sempre ligado a ações e projetos que visam a proteção deste eco sistema tão frágil e delicado, enxergando desde há muito tempo a ligação simbiótica entre as nascentes dos rios, seu percurso e a vida nos oceanos e mares.

Dedicated to addressing the global need for clean, accessible water through the research, development and commercialization of socially and environmentally sustainable water purification and desalination technologies.

SAROS (Swell Actuated Reverse Osmosis System) 
By leveraging one of the most prevalent sources of renewable energy, ocean waves, EcoH2O Innovations has developed SAROS, a mobile, wave-driven, seawater desalination system. Utilizing only energy found ocean waves, SAROS simplifies the desalination process by removing dependency on power sources and provide fresh water to island and coastal communities.

Current desalination efforts tend toward large-scale plants or solutions which rely on grid electricity and/or fossil fuels. SAROS targets areas where typical solutions are unfeasible or undesirable. On remote islands, technologies requiring a grid connection are largely unusable, and end-user simplicity and reliable operation are needed. Being wave- driven, the SAROS unit is capable of operating completely off grid. In other coastal areas, large quantities of water are required and reliance on large-scale plants powered through fossil fuels is environmentally irresponsible. Moving to diverse and sustainable solutions for water management, including but not limited to desalination, reduces effects of outside factors, such as oil prices and damages to the water supply. SAROS will be a key component of this diverse and sustainable water supply.

With this clean technology, we are expanding the water source, rather than reusing current water supply and bringing desalination to areas that otherwise lacked access. Water scarcity is a growing issue and the need for this sustainable, affordable solution will only grow.

PROJECT BLUE
The Project Blue water filtration system eliminates the need for destructive, local deforestation because it filters water to safe, potable conditions without the need to boil. Com base no entendimento de que parte das organizações não governamentais e das instituições ambientais trabalha  com uma perspectiva profundamente conservadora, no sentido de que não há um questionamento efetivo sobre as raízes dos problemas socioambientais, raízes essas que a nosso ver estão ligadas às relações do capital com o meio ambiente, com a monetização da natureza, com a privatização dos territórios e a transformação do trabalho e as relações sociais em mercadoria entre outras questões, um grupo de ativistas socioambientais decidiu pela construção deste coletivo.

Entendemos que reduzir, reciclar e reutilizar são ideias fundamentais, mas estão longe de resolver os problemas socioambientais. defendemos uma agroecologia – saudável, familiar e descentralizada – com distribuição da terra e reforma das questões agrárias. Acreditamos que um selo verde em uma embalagem de plástico não é suficiente. Nossa humanidade é muito maior que qualquer consumo. Menos é mais!
Assim, a Associação Sustentabilidade Popular vem para juntar forças com outros coletivos e contribuir na construção de uma sociedade baseada na igualdade e justiça socioambiental .

Description:
The proposed business of Super Intensive Stacked Raceway Shrimp Farming is a new technology developed at Texas A&M University by Dr. Addison Lawrence. We have secured an agreement with Royal Caridea L.L.C. to build a production facility in Western North Carolina. Our objective is to produce one million pounds of fresh organic shrimp and market it locally, with the intent to expand production as we move forward. Cost of building and operation until revenue can be realized will be in excess of 9.5 million dollars. We will be seeking investors and looking into Small Business Administration USDA loans for funding. Payback for this project is estimated to be 3-4 years with an average selling price per pound around $7.50 per pound. 
     Market competition is imported foreign head-off frozen shrimp. The US imports 5.5 billion dollars of shrimp annually from south East Asia, India and South America. Food safety is a major concern with foreign product. The ecological impact in producing countries has caused a decline in production in many of those countries. A devastating pathogen called Early Mortality Syndrome (EMS) has ravaged many production facilities completely wiping out shrimp production. Cost of shrimp has been escalating over the last few years and no relief is in sight. US pond farming has been on the rise, but is limited because of the low production rates and limited seasonal harvest. The production facility we propose is able to produce one million pounds of shrimp per year in staggered harvest in a climate controlled environment with automated feeding system, post-larvae nursery tanks, re-circulating filtration system and computer monitoring of critical metrics. The 20 stacked raceways will be constructed and consist of 7 rectangular ponds of 6-8 feet wide by 56 feet long  that will produce 428,000kg of shrimp annually.

Name: The Battery Innovation Center
Description:
The Battery Innovation Center (BIC) is a collaborative initiative designed to incorporate leadership from renowned universities, government agencies, and commercial enterprises to focus on the rapid development, testing and commercialization of safe, reliable and lightweight energy storage systems for defense and commercial customers.

The BIC’s mission is to accelerate innovation in the field of battery technology by providing access to the entire spectrum of R&D to commercialization, including low volume production, in a single 40,000 square foot facility. Under one roof and with virtual connections to partners’ research and manufacturing facilities, the BIC will be capable of managing all aspects of the battery life cycle:

- Basic and applied research
- Elementary cell concept
- Cell research and development
- Cell manufacturing
- Electronic control
- Pack systems engineering, testing and certification
- Low volume manufacturing
- Field service and support

Battery Center Mission Statement:

The Battery Innovation Center incorporates leadership from world-class universities and commercial enterprises to focus on the rapid development, testing and commercialization of safe, reliable and lightweight energy storage systems for commercial and defense customers.


Battery Innovation Center Goals:

1. Provide military and national security customers with a robust and secure source of battery development and low-volume production under one roof with linkages to an array of high-volume commercial manufacturing partners.

2. Give commercial industry a one-stop shop for battery testing and certification along with a full spectrum of world-class support services from R&D to manufacturing solutions.

3. Establish a network that would virtually and physically link university-led battery R&D and accelerate the transition from basic research to battery cell and pack prototypes capable of commercialization.

Name: CleanWave: A Guide to Success in the Green Recovery
Description:
The Climate Crisis is humanity’s greatest threat, but it’s also our greatest opportunity.  CleanWave shepherds readers through the past, present, and future of cleantech post-pandemic and offers practical tips for those interested in career opportunities, or those curious to learn more.

Bloomberg New Energy Finance projects that $10 trillion USD will be invested in new clean infrastructure over the next 30 years.  Readers will hear from industry leaders in their own words on topics ranging from personal branding to entrepreneurship to creating an equitable energy transition for everyone.  Understand how clean power fits into the post-COVID19 American recovery and environmental justice. Whether you’re mid-career, currently in school, or a recent grad, the clean energy movement needs talent, and CleanWave provides a clear pathway for entry.

There hasn’t been a definitive book written about Cleantech, specifically for job hunters, since Van Jones’ The Green Collar Economy written in ... 2008.  That’s several lifetimes ago in terms of technology advancement.  After all, from 2000 to 2018 US wind and solar energy have increased 4,000% and 55,000% respectively.  CleanWave is the how-to guide I wish would have existed at the beginning of my career as a fresh college grad in 2007.

The Climate Crisis is and has been very personal to me, and a driving factor in my decision to join the solar industry.  After visiting my father’s former home in Tonga, where the average elevation is less than 10 feet above sea-level, it’s imperative that I do whatever I can to preserve his legacy, and the legacy of my ancestors.  We are all standing on the shoulders of giants, so we might as well align with our passions, make some money and save the world while we’re at it.

This also prevents chemicals from being carried in the air to plants and trees that do not need such treatments or could become sick if exposed to certain chemicals.

Name: Vermont Green Building Network (VGBN)
Description:
Founded in 2002, the non-profit Vermont Green Building Network (VGBN) works with the building industry to achieve our vision of fostering green building in Vermont, thereby contributing to a thriving local economy, a healthy environment, and high quality of life in all communities.

VGBN is primarily a volunteer-driven organization, and the support of members is critical to our success in carrying out the annual Vermont’s Greenest Building Awards Competition, education and advocacy work. The founding members of the Vermont Green Building Network (VGBN) believed in the power of a networking organization to promote green building practices in Vermont. VGBN was formed in 2002 with seed funding provided by the Vermont Department of Public Service to bring people together interested in transforming the way we build – to share ideas, learn strategies, and connect with partners. The organization became a registered 501(c)(3) in January 2004. In April 2005, VGBN became the Vermont Chapter of the U.S. Green Building Council (USGBC), connecting us to a network of over 70 other USGBC Chapters across the country. VGBN remained the official Vermont Chapter of the U.S. Green Building Council until December 2015.

Our goals:
- Promote collaboration among individuals and organizations that provide or use green building services, products and technologies
- Advocate for green building practices and sustainable development
- Educate the public and building professionals about green design, construction and building operations
- Increase the use and sale of Vermont green building services, products and technologies
- Increase the percentage of ecologically responsible buildings in Vermont

VGBN offers educational workshops and networking events throughout the year in order to advance green building knowledge and awareness in Vermont. Many of our workshops provide continuing education credits for maintaining professional licensure, as well as LEED credentialing.

Stirling-engine Developer Qnergy Acquires US-based Infinia

TEL AVIV, Israel, November 21, 2013 /PRNewswire/

"Qnergy, an Israeli-based Stirling engine manufacturer and its U.S affiliate, has acquired the assets of US-based Infinia Corporation Inc. located in Ogden, Utah. Qnergy plans to integrate the core technologies and know-how of both companies in order to commence mass production of Stirling engines for various applications within the coming twelve months.

Qnergy (http://www.qnergy.com) was established in 2009 by Ricor Cryogenic and Vacuum Systems, a world leader in the field of miniature Stirling cryogenic coolers. Qnergy's technology enables residential and business customers to generate power and hot water on-site (Distributed Power Generation) with total efficiency of more than 90%.

The company develops and manufactures highly efficient, reliable and cost-effective Stirling engines for various applications such as: micro-combined heat and power (mCHP), solar power generation and solar CHP, remote power generation and more.

Infinia Corporation is an energy technology company, developing and manufacturing high-efficiency, free piston Stirling generators that convert readily available and low cost heat sources such as solar, biogas and natural gas into reliable on and off grid electricity. Following 40 years of its ultra-high reliability technology for the DOD, NASA and DOE, Infinia has recently launched its solar product - the PowerDishTM. The PowerDish is the world's first Stirling-based solar power generation system suitable for automotive scale manufacturing and deployment, from small distribution scale arrays to multi megawatt utility scale solar plants. Infinia filed for chapter 11 and pursued a going concern sale of its assets this past September."

Name: Befesa - Barnwell, SC
Description:
Today, the recycling of scrap steel is of great importance, thereby reducing the extraction of crude steel, preserving natural sources and thus protecting the environment. Approximately 40% of the steel produced in Europe comes from steel scrap recycled through the electric arc furnace process (EAF process). The gases emitted during the process are treated and cleaned, collecting 15 to 20 kg of dust per ton of steel produced. Of the annual production in Europe of EAF powder thus obtained, which contains zinc, approximately 70% is recycled in the Waelz process.

The SDHL Waelz process, – patented -, is the result of continuous improvement carried out within the organization, through innovation and optimization of the classic Waelz process. Especially in food preparation, recovery rates and optimization of energy consumption.



The recycling processes carried out at Befesa Steel Dust Recycling Services are considered the best available technologies (“Best Available -Technique” (BAT)), as stated in the reference BREF “Reference Document on Best Available Techniques in the Non-Ferrous Metals Industries ”, developed at the request of the European Commission.

In addition, this process has important environmental benefits, since on the one hand the discharge of this type of dust is avoided and on the other hand, the amount of primary zinc extracted from mining is reduced.

Thanks to the Befesa Steel Dust Recycling Services activity, more than 650 thousand tons of raw EAF dust, stainless steel dust and other types of zinc-containing waste are recycled per year. Since 2012, Befesa Steel Dust Recycling Services has operated a washing plant in northern France, which further improves the quality of the Waelz oxide.

There is a clear path to growing crystals with uniform resistivity, which can increase the cell efficiency by 0.15%, which has not been accomplished in solar manufacturing so far. The MLRC organizes activities of general appeal that draw people to the Center, where they are exposed to conservation exhibits and short presentations of communal interest such as LakeSmart practices, options for volunteer work, or where to purchase plants suitable for a rain garden and buffer strips. 

The building and creation of the Maine Lakes Resource Center was thoughtfully designed to bring disparate conservation organizations closer together, reduce redundancy, increase outreach, and grow capacity to reach further into the community; in short, to bring others science that can be used as part of their daily behavior. We are providing invasive plant identification and education to the business community and MLRC has provided a living laboratory for the Environmental Science Program at Colby College where future environmentalists are gaining "real world" experience on the lakes.

The	time	is ripe for	clean energy investments in this region; the	costs of all renewable energy	technologies	continue to decline, while the risks and	uncertainties of our	business-as-usual energy path increase	every year. In today's clean energy economy, businesses want greater choice when selecting energy suppliers to meet their	business and public goals. Businesses want access to	long-term fixed prices to avoid fuel price volatility as well as the	ability to drive	new	projects beyond	business as usual. In order to	meet their renewable energy goals, businesses want streamlined	financing	options	including	power purchase agreements.

Any one of these solutions may seem insurmountable	in Kansas	and the Greater KC	Metro, however, businesses	working together as members of the Clean Energy Business Council, can open up the market and drive innovation during the transition to a clean energy economy.

Name: Ndn Bayou Food Forest
Description:
The Ndn Bayou Food Forest began in 2018 during the struggle, led by indigenous women, against the Bayou Bridge Pipeline in so-called Louisiana. Water protectors set up camp and defended an 11-acre property from encroachment by the pipeline company. They forced the company to re-route the pipeline around them, while also carrying out over a hundred disruptions of construction elsewhere on the route. After the pipeline was completed in early 2019, water protectors shifted gears, from fighting against the systems that are destroying the Earth, to working to grow and build systems to heal the Earth and sustain life.

We want to make food free, especially in our underserved communities. That means diversifying local production - a field that once grew only sugarcane now grows avocados, sweet potatoes, mulberries, bananas, beans, kale, figs, catfish, okra, watermelon, squash, turmeric, basil, broccoli, cabbage, collards, and more.

Ndn Bayou’s strategy is to amplify our impact by producing & distributing not just food or medicine harvests, but the food & medicine plants themselves, thereby seeding not just one food forest but dozens, eventually hundreds.

So far, we have donated thousands of herbs, plants, and seeds. These and a diversity of other fruit, nut, & native wetland trees have been gifted to neighbors, gardeners, in neighborhoods throughout New Orleans and environmental justice communities across South Louisiana. 

Additionally, we have provided mutual aid support efforts in response to climate-related disasters within our local region. 

Every year, we find ourselves with a bigger surplus of consumable crops as our food forest develops and our soil improves. This year we expect to give away hundreds of pounds of greens, beans, squash, figs, avocados, bananas, plantains, watermelon, okra, citrus, and more.

GridThink is a clean energy start-up company that intends to commercial a novel  grid-scale electrical power product.  GridThink's grid-storage solution is clean, renewable, and best of all, inexpensive. We aim to store large amounts of electrical power for as low as 5 cents per kWh. 

The addition of solar and wind assets to the electrical power grid is accelerating a transition from traditional grid-energy to a distributed energy resources (DER) paradigm. Additionally, this benefits the decarbonization of grid-based energy production and helps to battle climate change and localized air pollution from traditional fossil fuel powered production assets. However, the episodic nature of wind and solar power production, and location of DERs bring new challenges in grid infrastructure, stabilization, and a need for storage. The grid storage capacity necessary to match this expansion is growing exponentially. There are a number of novel solutions, however, many have cost and scaling drawbacks. GridThink aims to deploy a scalable, distributed, grid-storage solution that matches the need for the renewable expansion and is both robust and cost effective.

GridThink is licensing the key technology from a DoD-funded, research and development partner, NDCPower.  The partner has developed an electrochemical-thermal technology storage mechanism, which was developed and perfected over the course of 8 years and with $20M+ in government funding and $2M in private financing. This phase allowed for the technology to be substantially de-risked and prepared for entry into commercial deployment.

The material is than composted through a heat process which benefits by killing weed seeds, pathogens breaking down the material into very fine compost. Even our binding agent for the pellets is a recycled vegetable oil. Our organic compost products provide organic matter, nutrients and beneficial microbes to make healthy soil. Another unique feature is we make and add in our own biochar. Biochar is a powerful soil enhancer that adds and holds carbon making soils more fertile. 

Quality natural compost provides soil with the essentials for growing healthy plants. Compost creates structure for the soil, making room that allows for water, air, and the roots to move more freely. It also allows for increased water holding capacity. Compost improves low quality soils by adding organic matter and nutrients. Plants grown in good soil are healthier and have greater resistance to diseases and insects. By reducing the need for pesticides and fertilizers you save money and plants grow healthier. Using fewer synthetic pesticides and chemical fertilizers also reduces your risk of contaminating drinking wells, local streams, ponds, and lakes. Most importantly not contaminating your family or pets. 

Using our products you can save time and money. Compost improves low quality soils by adding organic matter and nutrients.

Name: Klima International
Description:
We believe in a world where all people are empowered to turn the tide of climate change. 

Klima's mission is to support a sustainable and equitable transition to climate resilience for rural, coastal, and underrepresented communities through collaboration, education, and targeted action.

We have spoken with thousands of community residents throughout the US and global South about their needs and desires for their livelihoods and families in the face of climate risks. Through research, practice, and collaboration, we have developed methods to sustainably grow long term resilience in vulnerable communities. 

The core of our support is stakeholder engagement and local knowledge. We know that resilience requires rapport and trust between local, national, and institutional actors, and our methods provide the groundwork for collaboration, even with conflicting interests.

We use innovative, research-tested approaches to identify, assess, and manage climate resilience in socio-ecological systems. As an isolated community, it's easy to feel alone and unsupported. Therefore, we build partnerships between communities with education, workshops, and exchanges, to support sustainable practices and organically build community economic diversification. Finally, we work with communities to magnify their voices and acquire funding through multi-platform content.

MISSION:
Door County Thrive is a volunteer-run organization that strives to transform community resiliency ideas into action. We provide the opportunity for participants to envision and implement sustainable projects through self-directed design and strategic action. By empowering people through skill-sharing we aim to build an abundance of useful skills within our peninsula. We also emphasize connection by providing spaces for ecological organizations and individuals to grow into a caring and thriving network.

Keeping these goals in mind, we offer organizing, marketing, brainstorming, and networking. Leadership development will be encouraged for those who care to contribute their expertise. To provide a healthy forum for exchanging ideas we conduct informational meetings as well as casual potluck gatherings. We strive to keep the conversation growing and everyone connected to support the emerging culture of sustainability in Door County. Our strategy for implementing these big ideas take form in these three ways:

1. Skill Sharing Workshops: We encourage anyone with a skill or information they are willing to share in a workshop. Co-teaching or combining similar topics could develop from these suggestions. Skill sharing workshops will be hands-on, where participants can gain quality theory and practical application of the skill being taught.

2. Action Oriented Projects: Determined through group-based decision making strategies followed by the core group assembling, supporting participants identified and everyone will get a schedule. Action orientated projects are aimed at being highly visible and disseminated throughout the community.

3. Volunteerism: We seek to create a supporting body of volunteers who are aware of and can participate in events and classes that other organizations are hosting. This is done through networking, potlucks, engagement on social media and through the web directory of sustainability focused groups, individuals, and events.

Name: Arreola Soluble Solutions
Description:
Municipalities & developers are faced with aging facilities & infrastructure.  Cost of compliance is rising, and finding qualified staff can be challenging.  
Arreola Soluble Solutions is an independent consulting firm and was founded to help our clients overcome these obstacles.  Salvador Arreola, founder and Contract Operations Specialist brings 30 years of experience in Wastewater Operations and Facility Planning.  
As superintendent of a Class IV wastewater facility (with max capacity of 18.5M gallons/avg flow 7.5M gallons) he was able to hone his skill set.  Under his direction, a facility that was plagued with aging infrastructure, and ongoing compliance issues was successfully guided to meet permit guidelines within 8 months, utilizing an untrained staff of 9 people without major construction.  The facility is still meeting all current and future permit requirements – including limits set for phosphorous & ammonia removal and tight restrictions on effluent discharge.
This experience combined with Sal’s years of wastewater treatment operations, make him an excellent resource to help your municipality become a success.  We specialize in helping communities find creative solutions to get back on track.   We work with municipalities and independent developers/communities our services include, wastewater operations coaching and training, water reuse, renewable sources, Industrial & Dairy handling, community development & small neighborhood plants and lift stations, Master Planning.
We can assess current and future improvement plans to identify cost saving measures to mitigate expensive upgrades.  Our team focuses on helping facilities work with current infrastructure to get within permit compliance and reduce or eliminate costly fines (often in as little as 3-6 months).  
As an avid angler and outdoor enthusiast, Sal is committed to keeping our water ways clean and enjoyable today and for our future.  Contact us today, and let us know what keeps you up at night!
